newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Investigators to look for dormant Swiss accounts.
newsitem.headline: Investigators to look for dormant Swiss accounts.

text.p: Investigators will enter five Swiss banks next week to search records for dormant accounts of victims of the Nazi Holocaust, an investigative commission told an Israeli parliamentary committee on Tuesday.
It named the banks as Credit Suisse, Swiss Bank Corporation, Spar and Leihkasse Berne, Bank Cantonale Vaudoise, and private Pictet & Cie.

"Our mission is quite specific. It is to search for dormant accounts of refugees or would-be refugees who could not be refugees because they lost their lives," said Paul Volcker, chairman of the Independent Committee of Eminent Persons, charged with investigating Swiss banks.
Money discovered in the audits will be returned to Holocaust survivors or the heirs of the victims.
The audit follows revelations that neutral Switzerland bought looted Nazi gold and sold $150 million of weapons to Germany during World War Two.
Switzerland also sheltered 235 refugees during the war and turned away another 30,000, according to Swiss government figures.
Volcker said the three auditing firms conducting the pilot search would also look for accounts that should be dormant, but were plundered after World War Two.
"I'm sure it did happen," Edgar Bronfman, president of the World Jewish Congress, told Reuters.
Volcker also said he was working on getting the names of dormant account holders published. Bronfman estimated the number of names at 40,000.
A full-scale investigation of more Swiss banks will begin after a committee reviews the pilot results in September.
The entire auditing process should take one-and-a-half to two years, and victims should then be able to claim money. But the claims process could be difficult.
"A small part have documents to prove and ratify. But the grand majority do not have documents," said Avraham Hirshson, chairman of the Israeli parliamentary committee.

In the wake of revelations on Swiss conduct during the war, the executive of the World Jewish Restitution Organisation has agreed to establish an international commission of inquiry into European governments' financial deals with Nazi Germany and looted Jewish property.

"Not a single European country remains unstained by the plundering of the Jews. There must be a limit to their hypocrisy," Jewish Agency Chairman Avraham Burg, who proposed the commission, told the Knesset.
Hungary has already agreed to pay $26 million to its 22,000 Holocaust survivors. Hirshson said Norway is considering a similar agreement.
But he said the former Soviet Union had not begun to compensate survivors, and France had 2,500 looted pictures in its museums.
"Our greatest enemy is time. In five, six, 10 years from now, the survivors will no longer be with us," Hirshson said.
